chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Bukayr from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah ibn A'yan who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman who was in Iraq, then he traveled to Syria and married another woman, and it turned out that she was the sister of the woman he had married in Iraq. He said: 'He is separated from the one he married in Syria, and he does not approach the woman until the waiting period of the second one expires.'
I said: 'If he married a woman, then married her mother, while he did not know that she was her mother?' He said: 'Allah has excused him for his ignorance in that matter.'

Then he said: 'When he knows that she is her mother, he should not approach her, nor should he approach the daughter, until the waiting period of the mother expires from him. When the waiting period of the mother expires, the marriage of the daughter becomes permissible for him.'
I said: 'And if the mother bears a child?' He said: 'He is her child, and her son becomes a brother to his wife.'

key_terms.عِدَّةُ الثَّانِيَةِ: The waiting period of the second wife
key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْأُمِّ: The waiting period of the mother

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries two sisters or a mother and daughter without knowing their relationship?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* and tracing back to the prominent jurist Zurarah, this hadith elucidates the mechanics of *Nikah al-Mut'ah* or permanent marriage regarding the prohibition of sisters and mothers/daughters. It highlights the Shia principle of *Jahalah* (ignorance) exempting the man from immediate separation until the second wife's *Iddah* expires, ensuring legal clarity for lineage and subsequent marriage validity.
